scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9112: From my machine PC0 (20.1.1.10) I can no longer reach
PC12 (120.1.1.10) at all -- my pings time out, every single one. It was fine
before last night, so something has changed on your side. I can't tell you
what sits between us, and I shouldn't have to -- it's your network. Check the
path and get us talking again today, please.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12 (120.1.1.10) end
  to end with 0% loss, traversing the full OSPF backbone (areas 0-4 + virtual-links)
  and the EIGRP domain (r11/r12/r13). Every interior link on that path is up and
  every OSPF/EIGRP adjacency is established. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of a backbone link-down that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- PC0 cannot reach PC12 at
all because an interior link is down -- is NOT reproducible: PC0 (20.1.1.10) pings
PC12 (120.1.1.10) with 0% loss in both directions. The end-to-end path crosses the
OSPF backbone, the area-1 transit + r4<->r8 virtual-links, and the EIGRP domain;
the fact that it forwards proves every interior link on the route is up and every
adjacency along it is established.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: cross-network reachability is healthy
and the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the PC0->PC12
ping, finds it working at 0% loss, optionally traces the path or spot-checks a
couple of OSPF/EIGRP neighbor states (all up), and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a down interior link -- picking some backbone interface and declaring it
the cut to satisfy the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested end-to-end connectivity between PC0 (20.1.1.10) and PC12 (120.1.1.10). Both topology-wide reachability and targeted probes show the path is healthy now. From PC0 to PC12: 5/5 ICMP replies received, 0% loss, RTT ~0.7–1.4 ms, ttl=61. From PC12 to PC0: 5/5 replies, 0% loss, RTT ~0.7–1.2 ms, ttl=61. These stable, low-latency round trips confirm that the intermediate L2/L3 segments are up and forwarding without filtering or blackholing, and there is no current asymmetry or congestion affecting ICMP.

Affected component: none at this time; the network path is operating normally.
Mechanism: Since probes succeed bidirectionally with no loss, your previous ping timeouts are not reproducible now; there is no evidence of routing failure, ACL/filtering, or link down in the current state.
Localization: No active faults observed along the path between PC0’s segment (E) and PC12’s segment (GG); the routers in between are forwarding normally as evidenced by consistent TTL and RTT.
Root cause: No active fault found; the earlier outage appears to have been transient or has already been remediated.
Corrective fix: None required. Service is restored. If the problem recurs, please note the exact time and we will correlate with control-plane logs/telemetry and trace the path at that moment; we can also enable continuous monitoring to catch intermittent faults.
